metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code present (VB6 .frm file with entry point form) with a single deployable unit (Win32 desktop EXE). Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: The application performs CRUD operations on a customer database (INSERT INTO Customers) via a form-based UI. It owns persistent state (Microsoft Access .mdb). Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall Score 1.05 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings (below the 12 threshold) map to Remediation Required tier. The score-based assessment more accurately reflects this repository's state. The count-based tier is limited by the number of core questions eligible for High severity (14 total, with 3 surface-gated to Not Evaluated).

decomposition_strategy.rationale: VB6 technology gap makes Strangler Fig and modular monolith approaches infeasible. Build a parallel replacement web application incrementally while retiring the VB6 desktop app.

approaches.name: Strengthen as Modular Monolith
approaches.reason: VB6 lacks language features for proper module boundaries

approaches.name: Strangler Fig (Parallel Track)
approaches.reason: Cannot extract VB6 modules, but CAN build parallel web replacement

approaches.name: Conditional / Adaptive
approaches.reason: Recommended: build replacement incrementally, migrate data, retire VB6

approaches.name: Big-Bang Rewrite

decomposition_strategy.estimated_effort: High — 6-12 months for full replacement delivered incrementally

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute is a Win32 desktop EXE (VB6 runtime) running on individual Windows 10/11 laptops. No server-side compute, no managed services.
findings.gap: No managed compute exists. The entire application runs as a client-side desktop executable with no cloud compute involvement.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the application as a web service deployed on managed compute (ECS/Fargate, Lambda, or App Runner).

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: All databases are self-managed. Primary: Microsoft Access 2003 (.mdb) on SMB file share. Reporting: SQL Server 2012 with nightly DTS/SSIS sync.
findings.gap: Both databases entirely self-managed with no automated failover, no managed patching, no automated backups. Access file share corrupts monthly.
findings.recommendation: Migrate primary data store to Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL. Migrate reporting to Aurora read replicas or Amazon Redshift.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: Nightly DTS/SSIS sync job is a multi-step data workflow with no modern orchestration. No Step Functions, no Temporal, no managed workflow service.
findings.gap: No orchestration service in use. DTS/SSIS sync is a hardcoded batch process with no visibility or error handling.
findings.recommendation: Implement data sync workflow using AWS Step Functions or AWS Glue with proper error handling, retry logic, and monitoring.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. All operations synchronous. Cross-system data flow uses nightly batch DTS/SSIS sync.
findings.gap: No async messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Access-to-SQL-Server sync is tightly coupled via batch.
findings.recommendation: Implement EventBridge or SQS to propagate customer state changes to downstream consumers asynchronously.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network security controls defined. Database accessed over SMB file share with no VPC, no security groups, no network segmentation.
findings.gap: No network security at all. File share accessible to anyone on corporate network. No isolation between application and database.
findings.recommendation: Deploy databases in private subnets with least-privilege security groups. Use VPC endpoints. Implement network segmentation.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API gateway, load balancer, or managed entry point. Desktop application connects directly to database file share.
findings.gap: Direct database access from client applications with no API layer, no throttling, no request validation.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway with authentication, throttling, and request validation as the entry point.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling mechanisms. Desktop EXE with static file-share database. Capacity limited to single Windows file server.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling on any resource. File share database has hard capacity limit.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling on compute (ECS/Lambda), database (Aurora auto-scaling), and supporting services.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration. Access .mdb on file share with no automated backup, no retention policy, no restore procedure. Monthly corruption events with no recovery mechanism.
findings.gap: No automated backups. No PITR. No restore procedure. Monthly data corruption with no mitigation.
findings.recommendation: Enable automated backups with PITR on managed databases. Configure retention periods. Test restore procedures.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or Helm. All infrastructure manually created and managed.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure manually provisioned. No reproducibility, no version control, no DR capability.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in Terraform or CDK: database (RDS/Aurora), networking (VPC), and compute (ECS/Lambda).

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Compiled on one developer's machine. Deployed by manually copying EXE to each laptop.
findings.gap: 0% automation. Single developer compiles locally. Manual file copy deployment. No quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Establish CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild) with build, test, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Visual Basic 6.0 — no AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, unsupported runtime. Cannot target any cloud compute platform.
findings.gap: VB6 fundamentally incompatible with cloud-native development. No modern ecosystem, no package manager, end-of-life.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a modern cloud-native language: Python, TypeScript/Node.js, or .NET 8.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries. Single VB6 form file with embedded connection, hardcoded paths, inline SQL, all business logic in event handlers.
findings.gap: No module boundaries, pervasive shared state, complete coupling between presentation, logic, and data layers.
findings.recommendation: Design replacement with clear architectural boundaries: API layer, business logic layer, data access layer.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication synchronous. Direct SQL execution via ADODB. Nightly batch sync instead of event-driven patterns.
findings.gap: All synchronous with no async patterns. State changes crossing system boundaries use batch sync.
findings.recommendation: Implement event-driven patterns for state change propagation via EventBridge or SNS/SQS.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. DTS/SSIS batch sync is long-running with no status tracking or async pattern.
findings.gap: No async handling for long-running operations. Batch sync executes with no status visibility.
findings.recommendation: Implement async job processing with Step Functions or SQS worker pattern. Provide job status APIs.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API exists, therefore no versioning strategy. Desktop app accesses database directly with no service interface.
findings.gap: No API, no versioning. Schema changes break all clients simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning from day one (URL path versioning: /v1/customers). Define OpenAPI specification.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All endpoints hardcoded as compile-time constants. DB_PATH = S:\CRM\sales.mdb. No dynamic configuration.
findings.gap: All infrastructure references hardcoded. No service discovery, no configuration service, no environment-based config.
findings.recommendation: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or AppConfig for service endpoints. Implement environment-based configuration.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Data stored on SMB file share (S:\CRM\sales.mdb). No S3, no managed object storage, no parsing capabilities.
findings.gap: Data on legacy file share with no cloud storage, no accessibility, no redundancy.
findings.recommendation: Migrate structured data to managed database. Store any unstructured documents in S3 with lifecycle policies.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Database queries directly embedded in form code. ADODB connection and SQL strings in event handlers. No repository pattern, no ORM.
findings.gap: No data access abstraction. SQL scattered in UI code. String concatenation creates SQL injection.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository pattern with ORM. Ensure parameterized queries throughout.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: Both engines past EOL. Access 2003 (.mdb/Jet 4.0) is 20+ years old. SQL Server 2012 reached end of extended support July 2022.
findings.gap: All database engines past EOL. No security patches, no support, no modern features.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to current-version managed databases: Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL.

findings.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
findings.description: Application uses proprietary Jet OLEDB 4.0 provider and DTS/SSIS for reporting sync. No stored procedures in visible code but proprietary data access technology.
findings.gap: Moderate proprietary coupling through Jet OLEDB provider and DTS/SSIS ETL. Proprietary connection technology ties application to Microsoft engines.
findings.recommendation: Replace Jet OLEDB with standard PostgreSQL/MySQL drivers. Replace DTS/SSIS with AWS Glue or Step Functions.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Access .mdb uses trivially bypassable database password. File contents stored in plaintext on file share.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest on any data store. Access password provides no cryptographic protection.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS keys on all data stores.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No authentication. All users share same hardcoded database credential. No per-user auth, no OAuth2/JWT.
findings.gap: No per-user authentication. Shared database credential. No ability to attribute actions to specific users.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT authentication via Amazon Cognito or external IdP.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. Hardcoded shared database password. Windows USERNAME environment variable for attribution (not authenticated).
findings.gap: No centralized identity. No IdP. No SSO. User identity from Windows environment variable.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or corporate IdP via SAML/OIDC. Implement SSO.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in source code: Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw". Visible in repository.
findings.gap: Critical: plaintext password in source code and compiled binary. No secrets management. Credential in git history.
findings.recommendation: Use AWS Secrets Manager for all credentials with automated rotation. Rotate exposed password immediately.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy. Desktop EXE on individual laptops with no managed patching. VB6 runtime unsupported. No vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: No patching. No vulnerability scanning. Unsupported runtime. No security updates possible.
findings.recommendation: Use managed compute (Fargate/Lambda) for automatic patching. Enable Inspector. Use Dependabot/Renovate.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning. No CI/CD pipeline. Known SQL injection vulnerability exists undetected in frmCustomer.frm.
findings.gap: No security scanning. SQL injection vulnerability undetected. No SAST, no dependency scanning.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (SonarQube/Semgrep), dependency scanning (Dependabot/Snyk), and container scanning in CI/CD.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No observability instrumentation. Errors suppressed with On Error Resume Next.
findings.gap: No tracing, no observability. Errors silently swallowed. No ability to diagnose issues.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry from the start. Enable X-Ray tracing on all AWS services.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No monitoring. No definition of acceptable service levels. README documents symptoms but no targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs. No monitoring. No measurable definition of correct operation.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for critical user journeys. Implement CloudWatch alarms and error budget tracking.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business metrics tracked. No CloudWatch integration, no dashboards.
findings.gap: No business or infrastructure metrics. No visibility into system health or usage.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics (customers created/day, save latency, error rates) via CloudWatch custom metrics.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No anomaly detection. Only error notification is user-facing MsgBox. Corruption discovered by users.
findings.gap: No alerting. System failures discovered by end users, not automated monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on error rates, latency, database health. Enable anomaly detection.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README states: 'No tests, no build server.' Zero test coverage since 2005.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage. No safety net. No ability to detect regressions.
findings.recommendation: Establish comprehensive test strategy: unit tests (80%+), integration tests, end-to-end tests. Integrate into CI/CD.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no CODEOWNERS, no team attribution for service health.
findings.gap: No observability infrastructure to own. No dashboards, no alarms, no SLO definitions.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards with named team owners, alarms with escalation paths, SLO definitions.
